messages:
incident-bot: :warning: SEV2 GeoDNS/Resolver anomalies detected. Multiple external resolver traces show inconsistent answers for geo-records for inference-api.redwood.example. Rate of 5xx spikes in EU synthetic probes. Paging oncall (maria) and neteng.

maria: on it. seeing synthetic alert dashboard, p50 latency up 180ms and p99 errors ~4.5% from eu-west probes since 09:12 UTC. Which DNS provider is primary for geo? Route53 primary, CF as secondary for LB.

simon: I've started traceroutes and dig from several regions. Cloudflare edge reports origin unreachable for eu-west origins intermittently. Route53 health checks show flapping in the health-check logs.

lucy: support queue getting ~8 tickets in last 6m describing 504s for EU customers. No obvious pattern by customer. Adding note to all impacted tickets.

maria: quick risk/benefit check: we can either (A) reduce Route53 sensitivity (increase consecutive-fail threshold), (B) disable the health checks so Route53 stops failing over, or (C) force a geo-weight shift to eu-central. Option B is faster but risky if region totally down. Thoughts?

simon: providers sometimes report transient NIC flaps; when that happens the health checks can see intermittent failures while actual HTTP paths are okay. I'd vote B for short window while we confirm with provider. I'll open cloud provider ticket and share traceroutes.

maria: ok I'll coordinate disable. Running CLI now: ``aws route53 update-health-check --health-check-id hc-0a1b2c3 --disabled``. Leaving TTLs as-is for now.

infra-bot: Deploy log: route53-change requested by maria at 2025-07-11T09:18:04Z. Change ID: C1234567890.

maria: disabled the health check. Monitoring DNS responses from 8.8.8.8 and 1.1.1.1.

simon: seeing answers stabilize for most resolvers within two TTLs (~120s). Some corporate resolvers still cache the fallback. Error rate dropping to ~1.3% on synthetics.

lucy: support update posted to affected customers: "We observed regional routing instability; we've applied a mitigation and are monitoring. We'll provide a full update after further investigation."

support: flagging SLA-sensitive accounts. CS teams notified.

maria: provider ticket created: "Investigating packet loss toward customer-owned instances in eu-west-1. Noticed concurrent health-check failures." Ticket #PROV-9981. They asked for health check logs and sample pings which simon sent.

alan: taking secondary on-call watch for next 30m. If error rate goes above 3% re-escalate.

simon: running continuous resolution probe script and logging to s3: ``while true; do date -u +%s; dig +short inference-api.redwood.example @8.8.8.8; sleep 2; done > /tmp/dig_probes.log``. Uploading sample to incident bucket.

infra-bot: S3 upload complete: s3://redwood-incidents/1756009999/dig_probes_sample.txt

maria: note for post-incident: health-check consecutive-fail = 2 is too sensitive for geo failover; propose bump to 4 and add cross-resolver synthetic checks (1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8, 9.9.9.9) before automatic failover.

simon: provider responded: "We observed ECMP path instability to host set in eu-west-1a, engineers applying fix and watching." They put an update at 09:34 UTC.

lucy: dashboard shows error rate steady ~0.8%. Most customers healed. Closing active support tickets as mitigated with note.

maria: switching incident state to monitoring. leaving incident open until provider confirms root cause and we complete a short postmortem. Cleo from neteng? (not in channel) If not, Simon, can you lead RCA?

simon: happy to lead RCA and draft postmortem. I'll collate health-check logs, traceroutes, and Cloudflare origin logs.

customer-success: notifying top-10 affected customers with a personalized update.

maria: handoff to simon for RCA; alan on-watch for 30m. Will add runbook action items: 1) adjust health-check thresholds 2) add multi-resolver synthetics 3) document disable-vs-weight-change decision tree.

support: tickets updated and customers emailed. No open P1 customer escalations.

simon: provider final update: fix applied at 09:41 UTC, path instability resolved, they will provide RCA in 24-48h. We prevented broad failover by disabling health check; good tradeoff.

maria: thanks team. Postmortem owner: simon. I'll follow up on runbook updates and schedule a retro in next oncall rotation. :white_check_mark:
